items.statement: When setting up a cleaning procedure for a specific piece of equipment, take into account its material of construction, its exact design, how it is used, and especially the specific substances that could contaminate it; do not apply a cleaning procedure validated for one material to other equipment or compounds without this.
items.quote: In establishing an effective cleaning procedure for a particular piece of equipment, firms must consider its material of construction/fabrication, exact design, conditions of use, and, in particular, the specific substances that could contaminate the equipment.
items.condition: when establishing a cleaning procedure for a given piece of equipment

items.statement: Hold data covering material of construction, exact design, conditions of use and the specific potential contaminants to demonstrate that a given piece of equipment is cleaned effectively.
items.quote: Therefore, to demonstrate proof of cleaning for a given piece of equipment, firms should have data that relate to all of these factors.
items.condition: to demonstrate proof of cleaning for a given piece of equipment

items.statement: In cleaning validation, do not rely on rinse samples alone; also measure residue or contaminant on the equipment surface by a direct method, if feasible.
items.quote: For cleaning validation, rinse samples alone would not be acceptable; firms should also measure the residue or contaminant on the equipment surface using a direct method (if feasible).
items.condition: if a direct method is feasible

items.statement: Swab and rinse samples may both be used during cleaning validation, provided the rinse solvent has been shown to dissolve the residues of concern and is otherwise suitable for use on the surfaces being sampled.
items.quote: some firms use both swab and rinse samples during the course of their cleaning validation. This is acceptable if the rinse solvent has been demonstrated to dissolve residues of concern and is otherwise suitable for use on the surfaces to be sampled.
items.condition: if the rinse solvent is shown to dissolve residues of concern and suit the surfaces

items.statement: After cleaning validation, run a residue-monitoring program for routine equipment cleaning, with frequency and methods set by risk assessment, to show the validated process keeps cleaning the equipment consistently.
items.quote: For routine equipment cleaning after validation, a residue-monitoring program whose frequency and methods have been determined by risk assessment is recommended to demonstrate that the validated process continues to consistently clean the equipment.
items.condition: for routine equipment cleaning after validation

items.statement: Use scientifically sound sampling and analytical test methods for cleaning validation that give adequate scientific rationale to support the validation.
items.quote: the sampling and analytical test methods should be scientifically sound and should provide adequate scientific rationale to support the validation.

items.statement: Make sure whatever material is chosen for the water for injection system is suitable for its intended use.
items.quote: Whatever material a firm selects for its WFI system must be suitable for its intended use.
items.condition: for a water for injection system

items.statement: Make sure the materials chosen for virtually all production equipment are suitable for their intended use.
items.quote: Whatever material a firm selects for its WFI system must be suitable for its intended use. This holds true for virtually all production equipment.

items.statement: When assessing whether water for injection system piping is suitable, take into account the surface texture or finish of the interior wall (e.g., smoothness, waviness), its resistance to high temperatures and pressures, and its ability to withstand sterilizing and sanitizing agents and procedures.
items.quote: When evaluating the suitability of a WFI system’s piping, consider the surface texture or finish of the piping’s interior wall (e.g., smoothness, waviness), its ability to resist high temperatures and pressures, and its ability to withstand sterilizing and sanitizing agents and procedures.
items.condition: when evaluating suitability of WFI system piping

items.statement: Ensure equipment surfaces that contact components, in-process materials or drug products are not reactive, additive or absorptive so as to alter the product's safety, identity, strength, quality or purity beyond its official or established requirements.
items.quote: Equipment surfaces that are in contact with components, in-process materials, or drug products must not be reactive, additive, or absorptive so as to alter the drug product’s safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity beyond its official or established requirements.
items.condition: surfaces in contact with components, in-process materials or drug products
